hypothesis: A single shared hierarchical discrete representation can support robust context-only identification across wave and nonlinear reaction-diffusion laws when the generic local law is fitted in decoded physical coordinates with symmetry-aware spatial features.

shared_representation.normalization: single mean/std fitted jointly across both law families only for tokenizer training and token lookup
shared_representation.decoded_coordinate_system_for_dynamics: physical units via inverse shared normalization

transition_identification.features: 16 generic physical-coordinate features: constant; for each of the two state channels center value, D4-symmetric axial radius-1 sum, diagonal radius-1 sum, axial radius-2 sum; plus center monomials u^2, uv, v^2, u^3, u^2v, uv^2, v^3
transition_identification.feature_scaling: per-sequence RMS scaling fitted only from observed context samples; constant scale fixed to 1
transition_identification.fit: for each test sequence independently, ridge least-squares 2x16 local map from the two observed decoded-token context transitions
transition_identification.rollout: recursive in physical coordinates; every predicted frame is transformed through shared normalization, requantized by the same shared two-stage RVQ, decoded back to physical units, then used for the next step

frozen_pass_rule: PASS only if every one of the 3 fresh end-to-end replicates has requantized rollout MSE ratio < 1.0 versus raw-state persistence on all seven primary tests. No retry or replacement of a failed or consumed replicate.
execution_rule: Run each replicate exactly once in an independent process and persist its result immediately before starting the next replicate.
claim_limit: A pass would support cross-law context identification under one shared discrete representation without explicit law IDs, equations, or hidden parameter labels. It would not constitute unrestricted law discovery because locality, D4 symmetry, radius-2 shell structure, and a degree-3 polynomial center library are supplied priors.
